text:
jordan_acme: Hey — hitting a weird import failure after upgrading to redwood-py 0.9.0 in our Docker build. We install the package with `pip install -e .` and our service crashes on startup with ModuleNotFoundError: 'httpx'. It works if we build a wheel (`pip install .`) or if I manually `pip install httpx` inside the image. Any guidance?

elaine_support: do you have the install log / Dockerfile? does the error show at import time from an entrypoint?

jordan_acme: Here's the relevant part of the Dockerfile and the pip output:```
# Dockerfile excerpt
COPY . /app
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install -e . 
```
Pip output:
```
Installing collected packages: redwood-py, ...
Running setup.py develop for redwood-py
Created /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_py.egg-link
```
Startup error (trace):
```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_py/cli.py", line 12, in <module>
  import httpx
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'
```

jen_devx: thanks — this looks like the classic import-time dependency problem. If your package's console entrypoint (or module with top-level code) imports an optional/extras-only dependency, `pip install -e .` can create an egg-link but won't pull extras unless you include them in the install spec. Wheel installs will have built the proper metadata and extras are resolved differently.

jen_devx: quick checks: is `httpx` listed under [project.optional-dependencies] or extras in pyproject.toml? And is the entrypoint defined in `project.scripts` or `entry_points` referencing a module that imports httpx at top-level?

jordan_acme: yes, httpx is an extras dependency (`[project.optional-dependencies]
async = ["httpx>=0.23"]`) and the old CLI module does `import httpx` at module scope. entry point defined as `redwood = redwood_py.cli:main`.

mike_infra: easy workaround: either install with extras explicitly `pip install -e .[async]` in your Dockerfile, or change to `pip wheel . && pip install dist/*.whl` so wheel metadata gets used. Also you could add `RUN pip install httpx` as a stopgap.

jordan_acme: repro steps I used (minimal):
1) python:3.11-slim
2) copy repo
3) `pip install -e .`
4) `python -c "import redwood_py; print('ok')"` -> crashes with ModuleNotFoundError

elaine_support: thanks — filing as escalation. marking possible root cause: top-level import of optional dependency + editable install not installing extras. Suggest dev fix to lazy import.

jen_devx: I opened PR #412 to change the entrypoint to avoid import-time httpx. Patch moves `import httpx` inside `main()` and adds a small unit test. We should also update docs to recommend using wheels in CI/docker builds or explicitly including extras for editable installs.

deploy-bot: deployment attempt to prod failed (rollback) — service crashed on postdeploy smoke tests: 1/1 unhealthy.

mike_infra: temporary hotfix applied to prod image: we added `RUN pip install httpx==0.23.3` and redeployed; services came back. We'll replace with the patched release.

elaine_support: release plan?

jen_devx: cutting a patch release 0.9.1 with the lazy import and a changelog note recommending `pip install redwood-py[async]` for editable installs or using wheels. ETA 1 hour.

jordan_acme: thanks all — confirmed that 0.9.1 fixed our CI build when we switched back to `pip install -e .`. We'll update our Dockerfile to explicitly pin extras until we migrate to wheel-only builds. :thumbsup:
